text:
[NDBG.4.1] `ds_engine_rete_network` enumerates the network as nodes and edges
via two callbacks, `ds_rete_node_cb_t` and `ds_rete_edge_cb_t`. All three are
declared in `runtime/include/libds.h`, which is the authority on their shape;
this clause states what they mean and not how they are spelled.

`rule_filter` (non-NULL) names one rule, and restricts the enumeration to the
nodes the rule's terminal is reachable from: its terminal or terminals, and
every join and alpha upstream of them. It reports only the edges whose two ends
are both reported nodes, so a filtered network names no node it does not
report. A name no rule carries enumerates nothing. `include_occupancy`
populates the live fact/token count per node, read between pumps, the only time
the call is answered ([NDBG.1.2]); without it, every node's occupancy is
`UINT32_MAX`. A node's `id`, and
each end of an edge, is the decimal text of the node's `node_id` in the artefact
(`proto/alfa.proto#AlphaNode`, `proto/beta.proto#BetaNode`,
`proto/term.proto#TerminalNode`), which the program fixes and every runtime
reads alike; it is never a runtime's own internal label ([RARC.5.3.2]). `label` is an alpha's schema
name or a terminal's rule name, and `filter` is an alpha's formatted test. A
beta's `label` is `join`, and its `filter` is `join` where it carries join tests
and empty where it carries none. `is_negative` marks
NOT-beta nodes. Every string argument is valid only for the callback's duration.

The engine must report every node before any edge: the alphas, then the betas,
then the terminals. The order within each kind and among the edges is
unspecified. A `NULL` `edge_cb` enumerates the nodes alone.

A debugger that cannot get a network (e.g. a non-Rete build) approximates a
terminal-per-rule topology from `rule_meta` instead.
